page.layout: One page of text, single column with full-width paragraphs. Marginal notes in the left margin: "1470." beside the line "Bohemiæ Rege", and a note beside the paragraph "Ac primùm quidem". Heading "FLOS IX." with subtitle below it. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: de Augusto Cæsare scribit Suetonius, eum M. Antonio hosti judicato remisisse necessitudines & amicos omnes: atque inter alios C. Sosium, & T. Domitium, Consules: Bononiensibus quoque publicè, quòd in Antoniorum clientelâ antiquitus erant, gratiam fecisse conjurandi cum tota Italiâ pro partibus suis. Nec laude caret, quod de fide 1470.MATHIÆ Corvini Regis Hungariæ itidem scribit Curæus in Silesiæ annalibus: quòd cùm in civitate Olomucensi, ubi cum Georgio Bohemiæ Rege, Cruce signatorum armis in summas redacto angustias, colloquium instituerat, Rudolphus legatus Pontificius eum hortaretur: ut Georgii filiis duobus, Victorino & Henrico, (qui humanitatem & fidem Mathiæ secuti eò quoque se contulerant) quibus reditum non esset pollicitus, præsertim hæreticis, ancipiti bello finem imponeret: quandoquidem Georgii spes omnis à filiis penderet. Mathias torvo vultu scele-ratum hoc consilium detestatus: fidem suam non Bohemiæ modò, sed totius terrarum orbis imperio sibi antiquiorem esse dixit: & ut ab hujusmodi consiliis deinceps abstineret, edixit. Utique enim tam turpe est fidem fallere: ut ejus turpitudinis cogitatio omnem utilitatem, quæ inde promanat, longo superet intervallo.
main_text.head: FLOS IX.

head.i: In Principe domi sit sanctitas: fortitudo in armis: utrobique prudentia.

main_text.p: SExt. Aurelius Victor in Trajano: Duo sunt, inquit; quæ ab egregiis Principibus exspectantur: sanctitas domi, in armis fortitudo: utrobique prudentia. Et his tribus omnia ea continentur, quæ Principem suis reddunt carum & acceptum, fortunatas Respublicas, regna beata, & imperia florentia.
Sanctitas in Principe cur necessaria?Ac primùm quidem, etsi multis Principibus Senecæ illud arridet in Thyeste:

page.notes: Printed text runs into the bottom right corner as a catchword "—sancti-". The marginal note beside "Ac primùm quidem" is set in three short lines and was read as one note. Long s was normalised to s throughout, and u/v to the vowel/consonant form. Doubtful readings: the small-capital "MATHIÆ" is transcribed in capitals; "Mathias" and "Suetonius" were copied as printed with u for the vowel. No signature visible. The "Sanctitas" note overlaps the "cur" of the main line, so its exact wording is partly inferred from the drawn letters.
